communication_job: Present, in four slides, the strengthened argument that MWAA should not build the proposed data center in its currently proposed location off the RWY 1L approach / RWY 19R departure end at Dulles — leading with irreversible foreclosure of board-reserved runway capacity rather than the hazard list, conceding the genuine counter-case (the 2018 Western Lands sale and the revenue argument), and closing with the specific regulatory gate MWAA should demand. This is an argument brief, not a report on slides: one claim per slide, one honest counter-case, one ask.
audience: Airport executives and sophisticated aviation readers — MWAA leadership, planners, and peer airport decision-makers who know Part 77 and grant assurances and will not accept hand-waving in either direction.
decision: Whether MWAA proceeds with construction of a data center in the currently proposed location within the RWY 19R departure and RWY 1L approach surfaces at Dulles. The argument's recommendation: do not proceed as sited; require the full FAA gate for any resited proposal.
decision_owner: Decision-critical unknown: the run prompt names no accountable executive. The source argument is addressed to MWAA as an institution ('I recommend that MWAA does not move forward'); the evidence does not establish which MWAA executive owns the go/no-go on this land-use proposal.
approval_path: Coordinate the proposal with the FAA Airports District Office (the run prompt states this has not been done).
File FAA Form 7460-1 and complete the obstruction evaluation / airspace analysis ending in a Determination of Hazard or No Hazard (14 CFR Part 77).
Complete glare, thermal-plume, and EMI/NAVAID analyses and a stormwater design compliant with AC 150/5200-33C.

Evaluate the parcel under master-planning principles and FAA guidance (ACs, ALP SOP 2.00) and process a formal ALP amendment — the parcel was not designated non-aeronautical in the most recent master plan, and per the run prompt ALP review exists to ensure the project does not (A) materially impact safe and efficient aircraft operation, (B) adversely affect safety of people or property on the ground, or (C) adversely affect the value of prior federal investment.

Qualification: the run prompt does not specify MWAA's internal approval sequence (board vs. staff authority) for this proposal; that internal path is an unresolved authority question. Note also that Section 743 of the 2024 FAA Reauthorization Act revised Section 163 — counsel should confirm the current framework before formal FAA submission.
first_90_day_action: Withhold any approval resting on the circulated project email; initiate FAA ADO coordination; and direct Planning to run the tenant's actual site plan — structure and appurtenance heights, ground elevations, distances to the 1L/19R surfaces and the ALSF-2 — through a Part 77 / AC 150/5300-13 penetration analysis and an ALP overlay confirming whether the parcel sits within reserved runway-extension surfaces.
success_measures: No construction start, lease execution, or site commitment before ADO-coordinated Form 7460-1 obstruction evaluation, glare/plume/EMI analyses, a compliant stormwater design, and a formal ALP amendment are complete.
ALP overlay and Part 77 analysis of the real site plan delivered within 90 days, closing the biggest evidence gap (no public record of the proposal's footprint, heights, or distances).

This siting rejected regardless of individual study outcomes because it forecloses reserved 1L/19R capacity; any data-center development redirected to land confirmed surplus after capacity needs — the 2018 Western Lands discipline.
Zero exposure to the $1,000-per-day Part 77 notice penalty and no adverse FAA finding under Grant Assurances 19, 20, 21, 22, or 29.
visual_thesis: One cross-section of the last 3,000 feet before the Runway 1L threshold carries the whole argument: federal geometry leaves 25 to roughly 200 feet of air above this parcel, the airport's own board has reserved the ground beneath it for a 90-million-passenger future, and concrete is the one condition the FAA cannot waive.

signature_visual.concept: The control-critical band: a to-scale side-view cross-section of the final approach and departure geometry over the proposed parcel, showing how little air the law and the aircraft leave above this specific ground.
signature_visual.visual_spec: Horizontal axis: 0 to 4,000 ft from the RWY 1L threshold / 19R departure end. Vertical axis: 0 to 250 ft AGL, flat terrain at runway-end elevation (assumption stated on-slide). Layer 1 — the 14 CFR 77.19 precision approach surface rising at 50:1, annotated: 'a 50-ft object reaches the surface ~2,500 ft from its origin.' Layer 2 — the AC 150/5300-13B 40:1 departure surface, annotated: 'only 25 ft of allowable height 1,000 ft off the departure end.' Layer 3 — a 3-degree glidepath (50-ft threshold crossing height) drawn as an aircraft descent line with three altitude callouts: ~102 ft AGL at 1,000 ft, ~155 ft at 2,000 ft, ~207 ft at 3,000 ft. Layer 4 — the ALSF-2 approach lighting system drawn extending 2,400 ft from the threshold. Layer 5 — a generic 50-ft data-hall massing block with rooftop chillers/stacks placed at the parcel's approximate position, rendered in the accent color where it approaches the surfaces. Inset strip (bottom right): a 10,000-ft separation ruler from AC 150/5200-33C with the proposed runway-end stormwater pond marked almost entirely inside the standard. Single accent color for the aircraft band and massing block; all other layers in two neutral tones. No decorative elements. State on-slide: heights are derived from published FAA geometry, not the unpublished site plan.
signature_visual.source_note: 14 CFR 77.19 (50:1 precision approach surface); FAA AC 150/5300-13B (40:1 departure surface); FAA ALSF-2 system specifications (2,400 ft); FAA AC 150/5200-33C (10,000-ft wildlife separation); analyst constructions from standard 3-degree glidepath geometry, reproducible in outputs/stage1/quantitative-analysis/.
signature_visual.asset_source: Designer-built vector diagram from the quantitative-analysis tables; no site-plan data exists publicly — geometry is generic and labeled as such.

slides.narrative_job: State the claim: this parcel is board-reserved runway capacity, and a data center is the one commitment MWAA cannot undo.
slides.headline: This ground is reserved capacity. A data center pours the option in concrete.
slides.visual_spec: A single horizontal timeline, five nodes, left to right: 1958 (fifth runway in Dulles designs) → 1985 (carried in the master plan) → 2005 (FAA Record of Decision approves fourth and fifth runways) → 2024 (all-time record: 27.25M passengers; United ≈70% of departures) → July 16, 2025 (MWAA Board reaffirms master plan toward ~90M annual passengers). Beneath the timeline, one sentence in the accent color: 'The proposed parcel sits inside the RWY 1L approach and RWY 19R departure surfaces of this growing airfield.' No map claim that the parcel sits on the fifth runway itself — the argument is the 1L/19R surfaces and reserved extension capacity.
slides.source_note: MWAA, 'Dulles Master Plan Update Sets Framework for Decades of Airport Development' (July 16, 2025); FAA ROD 2005; FFXnow, 'Dulles Airport's 2024 Passenger Total Set New All-Time Record'; Simple Flying market-share analysis (United ≈70% incl. United Express).
slides.density_budget: Headline + 5 timeline nodes + 1 accent sentence + source line. No paragraphs.
slides.speaker_note: Open with the discipline of the argument: every hazard in the original review is real, but each is something the FAA evaluates and conditions. The claim that survives FAA process is irreversibility — this is strategic capacity land a governing board has an active, reaffirmed claim on, at a single-carrier hub setting passenger records. Capacity land is optionality; a hyperscale data hall converts it to cash for the life of the asset. Do not overclaim: the published fifth runway parallels 12-30; this parcel matters for the 1L/19R surfaces and future extension, which the ALP overlay must confirm.

slides.narrative_job: Carry the signature visual: show the unforgiving geometry above the parcel — the evidence-bearing exhibit that makes the mechanism understandable in seconds.
slides.headline: The law leaves 25 to 200 feet of air above this parcel.
slides.visual_spec: Render the signature visual exactly as specified in signature_visual: to-scale side elevation of the last 4,000 ft — 50:1 approach surface (50-ft object reaches the surface ~2,500 ft from origin), 40:1 departure surface (25 ft allowable at 1,000 ft), 3-degree glidepath callouts (≈102/155/207 ft AGL at 1,000/2,000/3,000 ft), ALSF-2 extending 2,400 ft, generic 50-ft data-hall massing with rooftop plant, and the AC 150/5200-33C 10,000-ft wildlife-separation inset showing a runway-end pond almost entirely inside the standard. Label the assumption set: flat terrain at runway-end elevation; generic massing, not the unpublished site plan.
slides.source_note: 14 CFR 77.19; FAA AC 150/5300-13B; FAA ALSF-2 specifications; FAA AC 150/5200-33C; analyst constructions from standard 3-degree glidepath geometry (reproducible, outputs/stage1/quantitative-analysis/).
slides.density_budget: Headline + one diagram + 5 numeric annotations + 1 inset + assumption line + source line. No bullet text.
slides.speaker_note: This is the mechanism slide. 'Even if it doesn't penetrate' is not comfort — it is a razor-thin margin: data-hall roofs with chillers and stacks routinely exceed 50 feet, and whatever rises from this ground (structure, glare, plume) sits in the band where an aircraft is barely 200 feet up. Claim the geometry, not a proven upset: FAA's own plume guidance rates overall flight-disruption risk low for transport-category jets — do not assert the plume 'will' endanger heavy aircraft, and never cite 4.3 m/s as an FAA threshold (it is Australian, CASA-derived). The geometry argument needs no such overreach.

slides.narrative_job: Present the strongest counter-case honestly, then answer it with its own best example: the 2018 sale is the rule this proposal breaks, not precedent for it.
slides.headline: The 2018 sale protected capacity first. This proposal reverses the order.
slides.visual_spec: Left panel — 'The counter-case, at full strength': four short evidence lines with figures: (1) 2018 Western Lands sale: 424 acres to Digital Realty, $236.5M (~$558K/acre), proceeds intended to hold down airline costs; (2) Ashburn next door carries an estimated ~70% of global internet traffic; (3) Grant Assurance 24 requires the airport to be as self-sustaining as possible; (4) FAA rates overall plume flight-disruption risk low, significant mainly to light aircraft. Right panel — 'The answer, from the same record': a two-step sequence diagram. 2018 discipline: build the fourth runway and support area FIRST → sell only the surplus that remained. Current proposal: sell the reserved capacity itself → foreclose the 1L/19R option for the life of the asset. Arrow styling makes the inversion visible; the accent color marks the broken step. Bottom line: 'Concede every conditionable hazard; you cannot condition your way out of an irreversible commitment of land inside an active precision runway's protected surfaces.'
slides.source_note: MWAA press release, 'The Airports Authority Announces Sale of 424 Acres of Western Lands at Dulles International' (Western Lands were surplus after the fourth runway and support area were built); Lightyear.ai Data Center Alley guide (~70%, estimated, widely cited); FAA AIP Grant Assurance 24; FAA Thermal Exhaust Plume guidance (overall risk rated low).
slides.density_budget: Headline + 4 counter-case lines + 2-step sequence diagram + 1 bottom line + source line.
slides.speaker_note: Do not caricature the opposition — this audience will test it. Concede all four points as stated; they are verified. Then turn the 2018 sale: the MWAA press release itself records that the Western Lands were the surplus remaining after the fourth runway was built. Protect capacity first, monetize what's left — that is the precedent, and the current siting breaks it. Use 424 acres (primary MWAA figure; the 433-acre figure is disputed). Do not quantify forgone revenue as fact — no dollar magnitude is evidenced for this parcel on either side.

slides.narrative_job: Close with the implication and the ask: demand the gate, reject this siting regardless of study outcomes, and redirect development to genuine surplus.
slides.headline: The ask: the gate, not a slogan — sell the surplus, keep the runway.
slides.visual_type: gate flow diagram with framed standard
slides.visual_spec: A five-step horizontal gate flow: (1) No approval on a circulated project email; (2) FAA ADO coordination + Form 7460-1 obstruction evaluation (skipping notice: $1,000/day civil penalty); (3) Glare, plume, and EMI analyses + AC 150/5200-33C-compliant stormwater design; (4) Formal ALP amendment consistent with the Dulles master plan — the parcel was never designated non-aeronautical; (5) Reject THIS siting regardless of study outcomes: it forecloses reserved capacity. Steps 1–4 in neutral tones; step 5 in the accent color. Right-side framed panel — 'Argue on the FAA's own standard (Section 163, as revised 2024 — confirm with counsel)': (A) materially impacts safe and efficient aircraft operation; (B) endangers people or property on the ground; (C) diminishes the value of prior federal investment — with the (C) anchor: two 2026 federal grants alone ≈ $64M, a documented floor. Footer line: Grant Assurances 19–22 and 29 bind MWAA (GA 20/21 trace to 49 U.S.C. 47107(a)(9)/(10)); the Authority holds Dulles under a federal lease to 2100, under active federal pressure to modernize.
slides.source_note: 14 CFR Part 77 (§77.9, Form 7460-1, $1,000/day penalty); FAA Airport Sponsor Assurances 19–22, 29; 49 U.S.C. 47107(a)(9)–(10); Section 163, FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018 (revised by §743 of the 2024 Act — confirm current framework with counsel); FFXnow / FAA FY2026 grants (~$41.8M + ~$22.1M ≈ $64M); MWAA History and Facts (lease to 2100); FAA Newsroom (DOT Dulles initiative).
slides.density_budget: Headline + 5-step flow + 3-line framed standard + 1 footer line + source line. No paragraphs.
slides.speaker_note: The recommendation is a gate, not a wall: require every study the FAA process demands, and reject this siting anyway — because no study outcome cures the irreversible commitment of reserved capacity. Frame the objection on the Section 163 (A)/(B)/(C) test the original letter already uses; it is more durable post-2018 than grant-assurance maximalism, but flag the 2024 revision for counsel. The honest claim is 'must not proceed as drawn without adjudication, and this siting should be rejected because it forecloses reserved capacity' — never 'automatically prohibited.' Close on the 2100 lease: MWAA is the steward of this airfield for 74 more years. Sell the surplus. Keep the runway.

Minimum text size 16 pt for callouts, 10 pt for source notes; source notes must survive print at 8.5x11 handout scale.
